resources.string: The server certificate is not trusted. Compare its fingerprint with the certificate on your server before trusting it.
The server key has changed. Connection blocked: verify the new fingerprint with your server administrator.
The certificate has expired or is not yet valid. Check the date and time on your phone and the validity of the server certificate. Trust cannot bypass this error.

The certificate or its chain has an invalid signature, a weak key or algorithm, or an invalid certificate authority purpose or constraints. The administrator must fix the certificate; it cannot be approved.
The certificate does not match this server address. Check the address and ask the administrator to fix the certificate names.
Warning: the certificate name does not match the server address. Approve the key only after independent verification.

Ask the administrator to calculate the SPKI fingerprint with the command below. Use meshcentral-data/webserver-cert-public.crt for direct TLS, or the reverse proxy certificate when a proxy terminates TLS; substitute that file for cert.pem. Browsers show the separate certificate fingerprint.
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER | openssl dgst -sha256 -c
Verify through an independent, trusted channel. A fingerprint obtained through this same unverified connection does not protect against an intermediary.
Compare this fingerprint with the certificate on the server through a separate, trusted channel.
A changed key may mean someone is impersonating your server. Continue only after independently verifying the new fingerprint. The previous key will no longer be trusted.
The current connection will close. You will need to verify this server again if its certificate is not trusted by Android.
The certificate issuer identifies itself as a MeshCentral root.
The certificate is signed by an unknown certificate authority. If the server uses a public certificate, its chain may be incomplete — fixing the server is recommended.
